claims.text: Overall tribo-corrosion degradation in high-entropy alloys is governed by the balance between mechanical passive-film removal and passive-film reformation.
The protective film is a multi-element passive film.
Sluggish diffusion and chemical stability provide the alloy with an intrinsic ability to reform its passive film rapidly.
When passive-film regeneration is faster than film removal, total degradation is lower than the additive wear-plus-corrosion prediction.
Fast passive-film regeneration reduces both the wear and corrosion components of degradation relative to their additive effects.
When mechanical film removal exceeds the reformation rate, the passive layer cannot keep pace and degradation increases.
The proposed initial material is a fine-grained, equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy.
The as-fabricated alloy has minimal pre-existing oxide films.
The passive film includes Cr2O3 and Al2O3.
Fine grains enhance the continuity and stability of the passive film.
High configurational entropy enhances passive-film continuity and stability.
Mechanical wear intermittently removes the passive oxide layer and exposes fresh alloy surface.
The high-entropy effect and sluggish diffusion cause rapid repassivation through formation of a dense, multicomponent oxide film.
At moderate wear loads, repassivation minimizes total material loss.
At high wear loads, film removal surpasses oxide formation and degradation approaches or exceeds the additive wear-plus-corrosion prediction.
The protective synergy holds at ambient temperature and moderate wear loads that favor passive-film formation.
The protective synergy may fail at elevated temperatures because elevated temperature suppresses oxide-growth kinetics.
A comparison among tribo-corrosion, static corrosion, and inert-environment wear-only groups can isolate the coupled response.

contradictions.description: Sluggish diffusion is invoked as the cause of rapid passive-film formation without explaining how slower atomic transport accelerates repassivation; the stated mediator and kinetic mechanism are therefore in tension.

The mechanism predicts restoration of a passive film, but the falsification rule treats film characteristics similar to static corrosion as evidence against dynamic repassivation. A rapidly restored film could instead resemble the static passive film, so this example is not logically diagnostic.
